title: hunch shared on an empty memory repo: strict pre-commit refuses the team.json commit it asks for
observation: Right after `hunch shared --repo <url>` against a new, empty memory repository, committing the .hunch/team.json that the command says to commit is refused by the strict pre-commit (`hunch check --staged --strict`): 'strict check could not refresh the advertised team memory (unconfigured); refusing a stale pass'. The overlay is configured; the remote simply has zero heads because `hunch shared --repo` does not push an initial overlay commit. After `hunch shared --sync` the identical commit passes. Mechanism: extractors/git.ts returns 'unconfigured' when the contract remote has no heads; cli check --strict requires team pull status updated|current. Filed as GitHub issue #427.
evidence: 2026-09-25 demo7 (explainer Ep7): git init --bare memory.git; hunch shared --repo memory.git -> '✓ published .hunch/team.json (commit it)'; git commit -> 'error: strict check could not refresh the advertised team memory (unconfigured); refusing a stale pass'
hunch shared --sync -> '✓ committed + pushed overlay store'; the same commit then succeeds (349591f)
